ops.title: Cleanup pause is undone only by an explicit resume; the daemon log names the caller
ops.body:
**Observed 2026-10-12** on the running v0.78.11 daemon (pid 36163): a queue pause set at 17:35 and again at 17:40 read `paused=false` minutes later, same pid.

**Cause, from source at 55b442d4 (v0.78.11) plus the daemon's own log.** Not persistence, not expiry.

- `Engine.paused` has two writers: `load()` reads the journaled switch at startup (`internal/cleanup/daemon/engine.go`), and `pause(bool)` journals the switch before flipping the flag. Nothing else writes it. There is no timer, lease, or TTL on a pause; `Tuning.AwaitLease` is the await-priority lease and never touches the switch.
- The only route to `pause(false)` is `Engine.Resume` <- `opResume` in `server.go` <- `Client.Resume` <- `ccx vcs cleanup resume` in `internal/cli/cleanup.go`.
- `server.dispatch` calls `Engine.announce` after every successful pause or resume, logging client pid, client version, and the client's parent pid and argv to `~/.daemonkit/a/ccx-cleanup/daemon.log`. `rg 'cleanup daemon: (pause|resume)' ~/.daemonkit/a/ccx-cleanup/daemon.log` answers "who resumed" directly.

**What the log showed.** Six pauses and six resumes all-time, every resume an explicit CLI call. On 2026-10-12 a long-running Claude Code drive root (the release-v3 drive) resumed at 14:39:25 and 17:39:02 with `ccx vcs cleanup status; ccx vcs cleanup resume; ccx vcs worktree rm --path <settled lane worktree>`, and a third resume at 17:44:00 came through `timeout 60 ccx vcs cleanup resume`.

**Why sessions resume.** A paused queue refuses every new removal with `cleanup.ErrPaused`, whose text is "the queue is paused and takes no new removal until ccx vcs cleanup resume" (`internal/cleanup/api.go`); `internal/cli/stackrebase.go` prints the same instruction for a completed conflict workspace. A session doing worktree gc reads the refusal and follows it. The pause is one shared boolean with no owner or reason, so any session can clear a hold another session set on purpose.

**Gaps, not fixed here.**
- `announce` logs one level of ancestry, so a `timeout`-wrapped call hides the real caller.
- Nothing lets a pause say who holds it or why, and the refusal text steers every blocked caller toward clearing it.

Options put to the owner: coordinate between sessions (no code); an owned pause that records owner and reason and that `resume` refuses without an override (changes `cleanup.Switch` and the wire, so `cleanup.Protocol` bumps); logging the ancestor chain or session id in `announce`.
